title: Lua: Tables
description: Write a Lua program demonstrating tables as arrays, dictionaries, and objects with metatables.

codeTemplate.lua:
-- Table as array
local fruits = {"apple", "banana", "cherry"}
table.insert(fruits, "date")
print("Fruits: " .. table.concat(fruits, ", "))
print("Count: " .. #fruits)

-- Table as dictionary
local person = {
    name = "Alice",
    age = 30,
    city = "New York"
}
print("Name: " .. person.name)
print("Age: " .. person.age)

-- Iteration
print("\nIterating fruits:")
for i, fruit in ipairs(fruits) do
    print("  " .. i .. ". " .. fruit)
end

print("\nIterating person:")
for key, value in pairs(person) do
    print("  " .. key .. ": " .. value)
end

-- Metatables
local vec = {x = 3, y = 4}
local mt = {
    __tostring = function(t)
        return "(" .. t.x .. ", " .. t.y .. ")"
    end
}
setmetatable(vec, mt)
print("\nVector: " .. vec)
print("Length: " .. math.sqrt(vec.x^2 + vec.y^2))

verificationTest: output.includes('Fruits: apple, banana, cherry, date') && output.includes('Name: Alice') && output.includes('Vector: (3, 4)') && output.includes('Length: 5')
hints: Tables are the only data structure in Lua — used for arrays, dicts, and objects
Use `ipairs()` for array-like iteration, `pairs()` for dictionary iteration
Metatables customize table behavior with metamethods like __tostring
`#` operator gives the length of an array-like table
